AI NEWS DAILY — 9 November 2026

TOP STORY
Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to an executive at customer Megaspeed, whom US officials reportedly assessed as working for Chinese intelligence. Huang will cooperate; three House chairs want him before Congress on 18 November, a day after earnings.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. OpenAI closed ~$11B at a ~$1.25T valuation, well short of the $30B it sought. Anthropic's expected IPO valuation slid toward $1T-1.5T ahead of a mid-November Nasdaq debut.
2. Mistral published full Mistral Large 4 weights: 1T-parameter multimodal MoE, 1M context, 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, modified-MIT licence with a model-as-a-service clause.
3. Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small, a 594B MoE pretrained in 68 hours on GB300 in NVFP4, with Apache 2.0 weights promised after safety testing.
4. METR's 11-week audit found Anthropic's research velocity running at ~1.9x its prior rate, roughly 80% from internal AI automating research, with much evidence redacted.
5. Safety results landed hard: a Lean-checked proof of a 2008 conjecture, DeepMind agents weakening legacy 1024-bit RSA, and OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber rated Critical after sweeping 948 Linux kernel flaws.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY: The Verification Turn
Why checked claims are replacing impressive ones. Vendor leaderboards saturate above 99%; Co-Design Bench, built from real coding sessions, finds the best agent fully solves just 26.4%. A number that cannot fail is not a measurement.

Read the full briefing: https://dilip457.github.io/ai-news-daily/
